overview: Nobatia was a kingdom of Lower Nubia with a major center at Faras, also called Pachoras. Its political history and the much longer artistic life of Faras must be distinguished.

items.text: The National Museum in Warsaw dates the rulers’ conversion to Christianity to around 548. Different historical syntheses give somewhat different dates.
A church stood at Faras in the early seventh century; an eighth-century cathedral continued the site’s religious history.
Faras cathedral’s surviving tempera paintings date from the eighth through fourteenth centuries. They belong to the region’s continuing culture, not wholly to independent Nobatia.
Locally made ceramics and clergy epitaphs survive from Faras. These document skilled work and named members of its religious community.
An older Library of Congress synthesis places union with Makuria before 700, while acknowledging interpretation. No exact conquest year is asserted here.
